description: Erection of 2 x two-bedroom semi-detached dwellings with associated parking, landscaping and amenity space.
decision_conditions: The proposed development, by reason of its siting, substantial footprint, scale, height, massing and inappropriate roof form, would fail to represent an intimate, subordinate or sympathetic form of backland development. The proposal would introduce a substantial built form into an area characterised predominantly by street-facing residential properties with relatively spacious rear gardens, where there is no clear established pattern of comparable backland residential development. As such, the development would appear cramped, contrived and incongruous, failing to respect the prevailing plot pattern, spatial grain, rear garden character and roofscape of the surrounding area. The proposal would therefore be harmful to the character and appearance of the area, contrary to Policies DMH 6 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One (2012), Policies D1, D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021), and

The proposed development, by reason of its siting, layout and the arrangement of the proposed access route immediately adjacent to the existing ground-floor side-facing windows of No. 34 Drayton Gardens, would result in an unacceptable loss of privacy and a harmful impact on the living conditions of the occupiers of that property. The proposal would fail to provide an appropriate relationship with neighbouring residential accommodation and would result in an unacceptable impact on residential amenity. The development would therefore be contrary to Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020).

The proposed development, by reason of the constrained and substandard access arrangement, inadequate access width and geometry, lack of pedestrian segregation, absence of appropriate lighting and surfacing, inadequate turning provision resulting in excessive reversing movements, and the failure to demonstrate that the access could safely accommodate vehicular and pedestrian movements, would fail to provide safe and suitable access for all users. The proposal would therefore result in an unacceptable highway and pedestrian safety risk, contrary to Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policies T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework.

The proposed development, by reason of the inadequate provision of private, useable and suitably enclosed external amenity space for Dwelling A, would fail to provide a high standard of amenity for future occupiers. The proposal would therefore result in a cramped and poor-quality external amenity environment for future occupiers of Dwelling A, contrary to Policy DMHB 18 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020) and paragraph 135(f) of the National Planning Policy Framework.

The proposed dwellings, by reason of their inadequate floor-to-ceiling heights, would fail to provide the minimum 2.5m floor-to-ceiling height across at least 75% of the gross internal area, as required by Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021). This would result in a substandard internal living environment for future occupiers. The proposal would therefore fail to provide high-quality residential accommodation, contrary to Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMHB 16 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

The proposed development, by reason of its inaccurate biodiversity net gain information, would fail to demonstrate that the proposed development would be able to achieve the 10% biodiversity net gain, in contrary to Policy G6 of the London Plan, Policy EM7 of Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 and the NPPF.

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and NPPF (2024).

This is a reminder that Under the terms of the Planning Act 2008 (as amended) and Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010 (as amended), should an application for appeal be allowed, the proposed development would be deemed as 'chargeable development' and therefore liable to pay the London Borough of Hillingdon Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) and the Mayor of London's Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL). This would be calculated in accordance with the London Borough of Hillingdon CIL Charging Schedule 2014 and the Mayor of London's CIL Charging Schedule 2012.
For more information on CIL matters please visit the planning portal page at: www.planningportal.gov.uk/planning/applications/howtoapply/whattosubmit/cil
